approach: Add a login probe to the agent driver and call it at three gates in `crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs`: at dispatch, before the producer, and before the verifier. The trait method `AgentDriver::login(within) -> LoginCheck` defaults to `Valid`, so `FakeAgentDriver` and every existing test are unchanged. `ClaudeCodeDriver` implements it by running `claude auth status`, the no-model-call check setup already uses (xtask/src/main.rs:788-806; docs/design/athena-v0.md:1768, E20). It holds the job only on a positive answer: `loggedIn:false`, or an expiry the output reports that falls inside the look-ahead. Anything it cannot read counts as `Valid`, as an unreadable free-space figure never holds a job (disk.rs:47). A `Lapses` answer becomes a typed `LoginHold` error in `disk.rs`, with a marker in the existing hold file. Dispatch holds as `dispatch_disk_gate` does (nothing committed, job stays Proposed). The pre-producer and pre-verifier gates hold through `hold_for_login`, built on `commit_hold` like `hold_for_disk`. The pre-producer hold creates no candidate and no resume mark, and the producer never starts. The drain reads a `LoginHold` as held and ends the batch with `Stop::Environment`. The existing mid-run 401 retry (claude.rs:473-533) is untouched. Round-1 findings: the verifier gate moved into `check_and_verify` in mod.rs, and the drain test into drain.rs's own unit tests. That removes `verification.rs` and `tests/drain.rs` from the file list. Three files outside the listed deliverables stay, each necessary (the decision "Files outside the listed deliverables" says why): `athena-agent/src/lib.rs`, `athena-cli/src/wiring.rs` and `athena-core/src/run/close.rs`. The `claude auth status` question is answered from code where code can show it, and the rest is a Host question.

decisions.choice: Files outside the listed deliverables: keep three, drop two (answers findings 2 to 6).
decisions.reason: Finding 5 (verification.rs): dropped. The verifier gate is a call in `check_and_verify` (run/mod.rs, between `replay_stage` at about :2264 and `self.verification_stage(` at :2271), where `closing`, `verify_dir` and the resume mark are all in scope; the existing hold at :2174 removes `verify_dir` the same way. Finding 6 (crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs): dropped. The drain behaviour is tested in drain.rs's own `mod tests` (:4963), whose `Steps` stubs (`Stub` at :4970, `World` at :6312) return a scripted `Run`. Finding 2 (athena-agent/src/lib.rs): kept. The accepted reading puts the check on the agent driver. `Athena.driver` is `Arc<dyn AgentDriver>` (core lib.rs:233), and the trait is defined only at lib.rs:145, so a stub can replace the probe only through a trait method. Finding 3 (athena-cli/src/wiring.rs): kept. Production wraps the real driver in `DeferredDriver` (wiring.rs:143, built at :211); without a forwarding `login` the trait default `Valid` would silently disable the gate in production. Finding 4 (run/close.rs): kept. `commit_hold` is private to close.rs (close.rs:216) and `hold_for_disk` is defined beside it (close.rs:177), so reusing the existing environment-stop path means adding `hold_for_login` there. Duplicating the commit logic in mod.rs would be worse.

rejected.why: It still edits close.rs and puts a hold function away from its siblings.

rejected.option: Put the probe in core as a free function that runs `claude auth status` for any non-fake driver
rejected.why: Core does not know the binary (`claude_bin()` is in wiring.rs:114), and no test could inject an expired login.

decisions.choice: The probe is a trait method on `AgentDriver` with a default of `Valid`: `fn login(&self, within: Duration) -> LoginCheck`, with `LoginCheck::{Valid, Lapses { in_s: i64 }}`. `in_s <= 0` means expired already. `DeferredDriver` forwards it and returns `Valid` when the real driver cannot be built.
decisions.reason: The default keeps `FakeAgentDriver` (fake.rs:79), nested runs (wiring.rs:189, fake driver) and every existing test unchanged. Only three `impl AgentDriver for` exist (fake.rs:79, claude.rs:473, wiring.rs:143), and the wiring one forwards. A test overrides `login` with a wrapper that delegates `info` and `invoke` to the fake driver, so no gate logic sits in the double.

rejected.option: A new field on `Athena` or `StateDir`, like `StateDir::with_free_space` (state.rs:233)
rejected.why: `Athena` is built by struct literal in tests.rs:202 and test_support.rs:899, and state.rs is outside the deliverables. The trait method needs no new field.
It runs after the stage is under way and returns a driver error, not a job hold. It cannot choose between a no-candidate hold and a kept-candidate hold.

decisions.choice: The real probe is `claude auth status` with an env cleared to HOME, PATH and `AUTH_ENV`. `AUTH_ENV` is `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, passed only if set. It runs under a 10 s bound with a kill, and stdout is parsed whatever the exit code. The pure function `login_from_status(json, now_ms, within)` returns `Lapses{in_s:0}` for `loggedIn:false`. It returns `Lapses{in_s}` when a numeric `expiresAt` in epoch milliseconds is present and falls before now plus `within`. Everything else is `Valid`: a missing `loggedIn`, a missing expiry, non-JSON, empty output, a spawn failure or a timeout.
decisions.reason: What the code shows about `auth status`: it answers JSON with `loggedIn` and the auth method in about 250 ms and makes no model call (docs/design/athena-v0.md:1768, E20). Setup reads only `loggedIn` (xtask/src/main.rs:793-796). A run from an env cleared to HOME and PATH reported logged in (athena-v0-review-2.md:90, R15). Agents get exactly `env_pass` plus the set `env_pass_if_set` variables (athena-agent/src/env.rs:70-79), and athena.toml:69 lists the three credential variables, so the probe sees the credentials the agent will. A claude.rs unit test pins `AUTH_ENV` against `include_str!("../../../athena.toml")`. No expiry field is documented anywhere in the repository, so `expiresAt` is read only if present and its absence never holds a job. The 'will expire within the stage deadline' half therefore rests on a field the code cannot confirm (open question 3).

rejected.option: Read the credentials file for its expiry
rejected.why: The design says Athena never reads, prints or stores a credential (athena-v0.md:1415-1416); the file's path and fields appear nowhere in the repository.

rejected.option: A real model call as the 'authenticated call'
rejected.why: It costs tokens at every gate, and the request asks for a cheap check.

rejected.option: Run with the full inherited environment, as xtask does
rejected.why: It would read a config directory or variables the agents are never given, so the probe could disagree with the agent.

decisions.choice: The look-ahead given to the probe is `min(stage timeout, LOGIN_LOOKAHEAD_MAX_S = 3600)`, through a pure `login_lookahead(stage_timeout_s)` in disk.rs. Stage timeouts: dispatch uses `job_plan.planner_timeout_s` when `jc.config.job_plan` is set (planning.rs:404), else `producer_deadline_s(&jc)` (producer.rs:51, `pub(super)`). The pre-producer gate uses `producer_deadline_s(ctx.jc)`. The pre-verifier gate uses `jc.config.budget.verifier_timeout_s` (verification.rs:246).
decisions.reason: The live athena.toml sets reader, producer and verifier timeouts to 86400 s (athena.toml:50-52) and planner and critic to 86400 s (:224-225), with the comment 'they do not stop work'. If the probe ever reports an expiry, an uncapped look-ahead of 24 h would hold every job whose login expires that day. The driver's own comments say the login 'normally refreshes by itself within minutes' (claude.rs:362-364, 498-500). The cap is a constant, not a config key, since the reading adds none. It is my choice, so it is open question 1.

rejected.option: The raw stage timeout as the look-ahead
rejected.why: With 86400 s it holds nearly every job if an expiry is reported.
The reading adds no config key and no governance file.

decisions.choice: The hold is a typed error `LoginHold { login_in_s: i64 }` in disk.rs, with the text constant `LOGIN_EXPIRED = "environment: agent login expired"`. Marker: `write_login_hold` and `read_login_hold` use the same hold file as the disk and slot holds (`state.hold_file`, disk.rs:264-331). `AnyHold` gains `Login(LoginHold)`, and `read_any_hold` (disk.rs:351) tries disk, then slot wait, then login. The text says the agent's login is not valid or expires in N s, to log in again (run `claude` once, or set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, as xtask/src/main.rs:800 words it), then run the job again.
decisions.reason: `status` shows a hold through `read_any_hold(..).map(|h| h.text())` (status.rs:1141). `go_job` matches `AnyHold` exhaustively (run/mod.rs:496-506), so a login hold needs its own arm, and the compiler enforces it. The single field `login_in_s` differs from `LowDisk {free, required}` and `SlotWait {waited_s, limit_s}`, so neither older reader parses it. The text does not start with `PRODUCER_AUTH`: this hold is not a producer 401 closing and writes no outcome, so `StopCause` (disk.rs:441-490) is untouched. The text still starts with `environment:`, so `is_environment_reason` is true for it. The text names no stage, since the gate also covers the planner and the verifier.

rejected.why: It says 'producer', and `StopCause::ProducerAuth` is documented as an API 401 of a producer (disk.rs:446). The hold is a gate before any agent runs.
`athena status` would show the held job as 'interrupted' with no cause.
scope_guard.rs:790, reading/retry.rs:311 and drain.rs:2731 all match on `StopCause`, and none can see a hold.

decisions.choice: Exits of each new gate (one line each). GATE 1, dispatch (mod.rs, before `dispatch_disk_gate` at :1092). Valid or unreadable: continues to the disk gate; no state changes. Lapses: `write_login_hold`, a `held       <text>` ui line, `Err(LoginHold)`; nothing is committed and no evidence snapshot is written (:1175 is later), so the job stays Proposed; `go_job` runs it again on the next `go` (:471), `clear_hold` (:1105) clears the marker once the gates pass, and the drain reads `Run.held` (:4726) so `ItemEnd::Held` (:1986, :2761) and the batch stop follow. Fail or error: cannot happen, since every probe fault is `Valid`. Interrupt: the probe is a synchronous bounded subprocess and the marker is written after it, so an interrupt leaves nothing. GATE 2, pre-producer (`produce_and_verify`, after the disk gate at :1890-1892, before `producer_snapshot`). Valid: continues. Lapses: `hold_for_login` calls `commit_hold` (close.rs:216): it commits planning and baseline records with no outcome and no score, writes the marker, prints `held`, removes the consumed resume mark and its hold marker (close.rs:236-239) and returns the `LoginHold`. The job stays Dispatched with no process, no candidate and no resume mark. `dispatch` drops the build folder on return (mod.rs:1396-1401; `BuildFolder::drop`, disk.rs:683), `reclaim_interrupted` (disk.rs:627) and the drain's interrupted pass read the state, and the next drain retries from the start, as for a disk hold before the producer (drain.rs:253-255). Commit failure: returns the context error 'job N was held for an agent login, but its records could not be committed' (close.rs:229-232). Interrupt, kill or timeout: cannot reach this gate, which is before the producer starts. GATE 3, pre-verifier (`check_and_verify`, after the replay record is pushed, before `verification_stage` at :2271). Valid: continues. Lapses: `remove_tree(&verify_dir)` as at :2174, then `hold_for_login` with the candidate and check records in `closing`. The resume mark stays (written at :1949, and at :2254 with recorded checks when every check passed), so the next drain lists the job as interrupted and resumes at the verifier with no planner or producer run (drain.rs:255-260). Commit failure: as above. Interrupt: before the verifier agent starts, so no verdict is written. Closing, landing and failure exits are unchanged: no gate sits on them. The planner and critic rounds are covered by gate 1 only (they start seconds after it); no gate sits between planning rounds (planning.rs is untouched).
decisions.reason: The brief requires a table of every exit of each new gate. `check_and_verify` has two callers, `produce_and_verify` (:1950) and `resume_candidate`, so a resumed job reaches gate 3 and no gate 2, because no producer runs.

rejected.option: Close the job as failed with an environment reason
rejected.why: A failed closing counts as an attempt and feeds the scope guard; a hold uses no attempt, as the disk hold does (disk.rs:56-62).

rejected.option: Put the verifier gate inside `verification_stage` next to the disk check (verification.rs:175)
rejected.why: It would make verification.rs a changed file. The gate in `check_and_verify` has the same state in scope, and its only cost is that it runs before `demonstration_records` (verification.rs:156), not after.

decisions.choice: Drain: a pure `held_by_environment(&anyhow::Error) -> bool` (LowDisk, SlotWait or LoginHold) replaces the inline test at drain.rs:4726-4730. The `_ if run.held` arm (:1745) gets a case for a reason starting with `LOGIN_EXPIRED`. That case sets the outcome to `LOGIN_EXPIRED`, uses the fallback text 'the agent login is expired or about to expire; log in again', and calls `self.set_stop(Stop::Environment)`. `Stop::meaning` (:1127) and the module-doc list of holds (:249-282) each gain one sentence.
decisions.reason: Without the case, the outcome would be mislabelled `environment: low disk` (the else branch, :1757-1761). `Stop::Environment` already means every later item would fail the same way (:1127-1128, set at :2733 for a failed item with the same cause), and each later item would otherwise cost a read and a probe for nothing. The batch ends with the held item queued, so a later drain runs it after the login is renewed. main.rs:280 (the drain help text) lists the causes of `Stop::Environment` and is left as it is, outside the deliverables; it stays true but incomplete.

rejected.option: Leave the drain to pass over each held item
rejected.why: Every queued item would be read and held again with no progress.

decisions.choice: The reader stage (`athena ask` and the drain's read of a queued item) is not gated.
decisions.reason: It runs before any job is dispatched. A reader failure comes back as `Read.error` (drain.rs:4661-4672), not as a job closing, and its entry points are in reading.rs, which is not a deliverable. The three gates cover dispatch (with the planner and critic after it), the producer and the verifier. In a drain, a queued item is read first, so an expired login shows first as a reader error. This is a scope question for the user (open question 2).

rejected.why: There is no job to hold at that point, it needs a second hold shape, and it widens the change past the files the brief lists.

decisions.choice: The tests are fixtures over production entry points with a scripted stub, not logic in the double.
decisions.reason: `StubLogin` (tests.rs, new) wraps `athena.driver`: `info` and `invoke` go to the fake driver, and `login` pops scripted answers (the last one repeats) and records each `within` and the call count. It decides nothing. The core tests drive `Athena::go` with `athena_with(.., counting(counts, Some(root)))` (tests.rs:192, :3485), which exist today. The drain test uses a `Steps` stub in drain.rs's own `mod tests`.

rejected.option: A stub that holds the job itself
rejected.why: Gate logic would sit in the double, and removing the production call would not fail the test.

files.purpose: Add `LoginCheck { Valid, Lapses { in_s: i64 } }` and the default method `AgentDriver::login(&self, within: Duration) -> LoginCheck` (default `Valid`), with a doc comment and a unit test of the default. Not a listed deliverable; needed because the trait is defined only here.

Add the pure `login_from_status`, `ClaudeCodeDriver::login` and `login_probe(bin, within, wait)` (`claude auth status` under a bounded wait, stdout parsed whatever the exit code), `AUTH_ENV` and `LOGIN_PROBE_WAIT`, with unit tests on JSON fixtures and a shell stand-in. `invoke` and `retry_after_login_expiry` are untouched.

`DeferredDriver` forwards `login` to the real driver and returns `Valid` when the driver cannot be built; unit tests. Not a listed deliverable; without the forward the production gate would be disabled by the trait default.

Add `LOGIN_EXPIRED`, `LOGIN_LOOKAHEAD_MAX_S`, `login_lookahead`, `LoginHold` (text, Display, Error), `write_login_hold`/`read_login_hold`, `AnyHold::Login`, `Athena::login_gate`, a module-doc paragraph on the hold, and unit tests.
Add `hold_for_login` beside `hold_for_disk`, built on `commit_hold`. Not a listed deliverable; `commit_hold` is private to this file.

Call `login_gate` in `dispatch` (before `dispatch_disk_gate`, writing the marker and returning `Err(LoginHold)`), in `produce_and_verify` (after the disk gate, before `producer_snapshot`, returning `hold_for_login`) and in `check_and_verify` (before `verification_stage`, removing `verify_dir` first); add the `AnyHold::Login` arm in `go_job` (:496).

Add `held_by_environment` (LowDisk, SlotWait or LoginHold) used by `Steps::run`; a `LOGIN_EXPIRED` case in the held arm that sets `Stop::Environment`; one sentence in `Stop::meaning` and one bullet in the module-doc list of holds; unit tests in its `mod tests`.
One new entry at the top of `### Added` under `## [Unreleased]`, with root cause, fix, limits and tests. No existing line is edited.
Append D190 after D189 with Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and a Provenance bullet. No existing entry is edited.

steps: Step 1, crates/athena-agent/src/lib.rs: add `pub enum LoginCheck { Valid, Lapses { in_s: i64 } }` (documented: `Lapses` means the login is expired already, `in_s` <= 0, or expires within `within`; an unreadable answer is `Valid`) and the default method `fn login(&self, _within: std::time::Duration) -> LoginCheck { LoginCheck::Valid }` on `AgentDriver` (:145). Add a unit test of the default.

Step 2, crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs: add `AUTH_ENV` (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`), `LOGIN_PROBE_WAIT` (10 s), the pure `pub fn login_from_status(json: &str, now_ms: i64, within: Duration) -> LoginCheck` and `fn login_probe(bin: &Path, within: Duration, wait: Duration) -> LoginCheck`. The probe runs `<bin> auth status` with `env_clear`, HOME and PATH (as `claude_version` does at :66-77) and the set `AUTH_ENV` variables, stderr null and stdout piped. It polls `try_wait` up to `wait`, kills on timeout (timeout gives `Valid`), and parses stdout whatever the exit code. Forward `login` from the `AgentDriver for ClaudeCodeDriver` impl (:473). Leave `invoke` and `retry_after_login_expiry` untouched. Unit tests: loggedIn false, loggedIn true, `expiresAt` inside and beyond `within`, string or negative `expiresAt` handled without a panic, garbage, empty, a missing binary, a slow stand-in with a short wait, and `auth_env_is_listed_in_the_repository_env_pass_if_set` (an `include_str!` of athena.toml).

Step 3, crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs: add `LOGIN_EXPIRED`, `LOGIN_LOOKAHEAD_MAX_S = 3600`, `pub fn login_lookahead(stage_timeout_s: u64) -> Duration`, `LoginHold { login_in_s: i64 }` (Serialize, Deserialize, Display, Error, `text()`), `write_login_hold`, `read_login_hold`, `AnyHold::Login` with its `text()`, `read_any_hold` extended, and `Athena::login_gate(&self, stage_timeout_s: u64) -> Option<LoginHold>` (asks `self.driver.login(login_lookahead(..))`). Add a module-doc paragraph. Unit tests: `login_hold_text_tells_the_user_to_log_in_again_and_is_an_environment_stop` (text, `StopCause::of`, `is_environment_reason`), `login_marker_is_read_only_as_a_login_hold`, and `login_lookahead_is_the_stage_timeout_capped`.

Step 4, crates/athena-cli/src/wiring.rs: forward `login` in `DeferredDriver` (:143) with the same `get_or_init` as `invoke`, returning `Valid` when the driver is an `Err`. Add the two wiring unit tests.

Step 5, crates/athena-core/src/run/close.rs: add `pub(super) fn hold_for_login(&self, ctx, closing, hold: LoginHold) -> anyhow::Error` next to `hold_for_disk` (:177). It calls `commit_hold(ctx, closing, &hold.text(), "an agent login", |id| write_login_hold(&self.state, id, &hold))` and returns `hold.into()` on success or the commit error. It creates no candidate and no resume mark.

Step 6, crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs: (a) in `dispatch`, before `dispatch_disk_gate` (:1092), call `self.login_gate(first_stage_timeout)` (`job_plan.planner_timeout_s` if `jc.config.job_plan` is set, else `producer_deadline_s(&jc)`); on `Some(hold)` call `write_login_hold`, print `held       {text}` and `return Err(hold.into())`. (b) In `produce_and_verify`, after the disk gate (:1890-1892), call `login_gate(producer_deadline_s(ctx.jc))` and `return Err(self.hold_for_login(ctx, closing, hold))`. (c) In `check_and_verify`, after the replay record is pushed and before `self.verification_stage(` (:2271), call `login_gate(jc.config.budget.verifier_timeout_s)`; on `Some` remove `verify_dir` (as :2174) and `return Err(self.hold_for_login(ctx, closing, hold))`. (d) Add the `AnyHold::Login` arm in `go_job` (:496-506), refusing a held job with the hold text and the way to resume it.

Step 7, crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs: add `StubLogin` (wraps `Arc<dyn AgentDriver>`; `info` and `invoke` delegate; `login` pops scripted answers, the last repeats, and records every `within`) and the four tests named under criteria 3 and 4. Add `StubLogin` as `athena.driver = Arc::new(StubLogin { inner: athena.driver.clone(), .. })` after `ask`. For each of the first three tests, comment out its `login_gate` call, run the test, see it fail, then restore the call.

Step 8, crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs: add `fn held_by_environment(error: &anyhow::Error) -> bool` and use it in `Steps::run` (:4726-4730). In the held arm (:1745) add the `LOGIN_EXPIRED` case (outcome `LOGIN_EXPIRED`, fallback 'the agent login is expired or about to expire; log in again', `self.set_stop(Stop::Environment)`). Add one sentence to `Stop::meaning` for `Environment` (:1127) and one bullet beside the low-disk and slot-wait bullets in the module doc (:249-266). Add the two unit tests in `mod tests`.

Step 9: CHANGELOG.md: insert one entry at the top of `### Added` (after the heading at :35). docs/decisions.md: append D190 after D189 (ends :5633) with Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance. The Provenance bullet lists what was read (disk.rs, close.rs, run/mod.rs, claude.rs, wiring.rs, drain.rs, xtask/src/main.rs:788-806, athena-v0.md E20) and what ran. It says what was not measured: a live `auth status` output or an expiry field, how often the gate holds a job that would have run, the probe's cost, and the reader stage left ungated.

Step 10: run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`, each on its own, and fix what they report. No external service, CI run or push is involved; all tests run offline against stubs.

risks.risk: False holds: if `auth status` reports `loggedIn:false` for a refreshable expired access token, or an `expiresAt` that Claude Code would have refreshed during the run, a drain stops with `Stop::Environment` for nothing.
risks.mitigation: Only a positive reading holds; unreadable, unparseable or missing answers are Valid. The look-ahead is capped at 3600 s, not 24 h. A hold uses no attempt and clears itself once the gate passes. The behaviour of `auth status` is open question 3. D190 records that no live output was observed.

risks.risk: The real probe is untested against the real Claude Code binary; tests run offline against stubs.
risks.mitigation: The JSON decision is a pure function covered on fixtures; the process wrapper is tested on a shell stand-in (loggedIn false and true, garbage, missing binary, a stand-in slower than the wait); the wiring test proves the forward. The Provenance bullet states what was not observed.

risks.risk: If `DeferredDriver` stopped forwarding `login`, the gate would silently disable itself in production, because the trait default is Valid.
risks.mitigation: A wiring unit test with a stand-in-backed driver fails when the forward is missing; `grep impl AgentDriver for` shows exactly three impls.

risks.risk: An expired login also fails the reader first in a drain (reader error, outside this change), and the main.rs:280 help text for `Stop::Environment` does not mention the new cause.
risks.mitigation: Both are named in open question 2 and in the decision on the drain; the module doc and `Stop::meaning` carry the new cause. D190 lists the reader as not gated.

risks.risk: Gate 3 runs before `demonstration_records` (verification.rs:156), so a login that expires during those builds is not caught there.
risks.mitigation: The look-ahead of the verifier timeout (capped) covers the later start; a 401 mid-run is still caught by the existing retry and the closing as `environment: producer login expired`, which this change does not touch. D190 states the placement.

risks.risk: The probe spawns one process at each of three gates per job, adding latency (about 250 ms each, per E20, an estimate and not measured here).
risks.mitigation: No model call; a hang is bounded at 10 s and counts as Valid.

risks.risk: The D190 entry and the module-doc edits could trip the decision-link, governed-path or boundary-word checks.
risks.mitigation: Write D190 in D189's layout, append only, no Amends or Supersedes phrase, name the governed paths, avoid banned words and email-like text, and run the whole `cargo test --locked`.

open_questions: User: The look-ahead is the stage timeout capped at 3600 s (`LOGIN_LOOKAHEAD_MAX_S`), because the live stage timeouts are 86400 s (athena.toml:50-52, 224-225) and the cap only matters if the probe reports an expiry. Do you want a different cap, or the raw stage timeout (which would hold nearly every job if an expiry is reported)?

User: The reader stage (`athena ask` and the drain's read of a queued item) is not gated, because it runs before a job exists and its failure is a `Read.error`, not a job hold (drain.rs:4661-4672); its entry points are in reading.rs, outside the deliverables. In a drain with an expired login the first failure is therefore still a reader error. Do you want a login check there too, in a follow-up?

Host: Does `claude auth status` at the pinned Claude Code 2.1.302 (athena.toml:60) print a login expiry time, and does it report `loggedIn:false` for an access token that has expired but could be refreshed? The code settles part of this: the repository documents only `loggedIn` and the auth method in that output (docs/design/athena-v0.md:1768; xtask/src/main.rs:793-796), and the driver's comments say the login normally refreshes by itself (claude.rs:362-364, 498-500). The code cannot show the expiry field's name or whether a refreshable login reads as logged out. The plan reads `expiresAt` (epoch ms) only if present and treats everything else as Valid, so the gate never holds on what it cannot read.
